headline: Low interaction risk overall: no shared write channels or network egress, but prompt-injection and cascading-error paths remain possible through manual file/audio handoff.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Neither agent has a shared automated channel: agent_a has no io_surfaces and agent_b has no clipboard, stdin/stdout, MCP, or filesystem read/write. The only plausible bridge is manual transfer of content, so prompt injection is possible but requires unusual operator handling and the blast radius is limited.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies agent_a output into agent_b input or a file consumed by agent_b, injection becomes possible.
IF agent_b is wrapped in a parser that treats copied text as instructions, the risk increases.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate work queues.
Do not paste agent_a output into agent_b prompts without sanitizing.
Use a fixed template for any handoff text.
Add a human review step before any instruction-like content is forwarded.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a reports network_egress:none and agent_b reports network_egress:none, while agent_b also cannot read_filesystem or use stdin/stdout. With no shared workspace or outbound transport, sensitive data leakage between them is not a default pathway; only manual transfer would create exposure.
conditions: IF an operator manually transfers sensitive text or audio-derived transcripts between the agents, leakage becomes possible.
IF a shared external storage location is introduced, the risk increases.
mitigations: Avoid placing sensitive data in shared folders.
Use separate local workspaces.
Redact secrets before any manual transfer.
Disable ad hoc copy/paste between workflows.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a exposes no write or shell capabilities in the profile, and agent_b explicitly cannot write_filesystem, modify_git_state, execute_shell, or spawn_subprocesses. There is no overlapping mutable resource or write surface documented, so a capability conflict pathway is provably blocked by the profiles.
conditions: IF agent_a is later given filesystem or git write access, conflict risk would need reevaluation.
IF agent_b is reconfigured with write permissions, overlapping writes could emerge.
mitigations: Keep agent_b read-only.
Do not grant agent_a filesystem or git write access.
Document any future mutable resource sharing.
Reassess if either agent gains write permissions.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A cascading path exists only if agent_a's generated text is manually treated as authoritative by agent_b or an operator. agent_b has no action-taking tools or network egress, so the blast radius is limited to incorrect downstream text or transcripts rather than external actions.
conditions: IF agent_b is used to transform agent_a output into customer-facing text without verification, errors can cascade.
IF an operator relies on agent_a output as ground truth, downstream mistakes become more likely.
mitigations: Require verification before reuse of agent_a output.
Add a checklist for factual claims.
Keep agent_b in a review-only role.
Flag any unverified content before publication.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance mismatch is documented: agent_a touches no data classes and agent_b only touches audio and speech. Both profiles show no network egress and no secrets or OAuth scopes, so there is no evidenced residency, retention, or regulated-data violation pathway in this pair.
conditions: IF regulated data is later introduced into either agent's workflow, compliance must be reassessed.
IF a jurisdiction-specific retention policy is added, mismatch risk could appear.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair.
Record data-class handling rules.
Review retention settings before deployment.
Reassess if OAuth scopes or secrets are added.
